title: SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety after receiving subpoena
source_used: New York Post (own reporting, citing Council Speaker Julie Menin); International Business Times UK
key_facts: SpaceX agreed on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) to testify before the New York City Council about AI-related safety risks after being subpoenaed, according to Council Speaker Julie Menin (NY Post).
SpaceX is to send a representative this coming Friday (16 Oct), at 10am Eastern Time (IBTimes UK); it is unclear who will represent the company.
The Council issued the subpoena on 28 Sep 2026; SpaceX ignored it and the Council warned it would petition the New York State Supreme Court to enforce it.

SpaceX skipped the Council's first AI safety hearing on 5 Oct, at which officials of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta appeared virtually, along with safety experts and whistleblowers such as ex-Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon.
Menin called SpaceX's absence 'unacceptable' and said 'Self-regulation is not enough'.

Carmen De La Rosa, chair of the Council's technology committee, said SpaceX had 'tried to circumvent our city's public conversation on the dangers of AI' and pointed to the spread of Musk's technology at federal level.
SpaceX consists of Elon Musk's rocket and satellite business and his xAI AI unit; it went public in June (NY Post).
quote_evidence: Elon Musk’s SpaceX agreed Tuesday to testify before the New York City Council about AI-related safety risks after being slapped with a subpoena, according to Council Speaker Julie Menin.
“Self-regulation is not enough, and I am glad that we have now secured SpaceXAI’s commitment to appear before the public in the coming week,” Menin added.
why_it_matters_hint: A city council used a subpoena to make a major AI company appear and answer questions on safety.
event_date: Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 (agreement); hearing due Friday 16 Oct 2026.
